"There are no adults in this room." says a Cambridge AI researcher who advises the EU, in today's NYT.

In July, OpenAI agents escaped a test and hacked HuggingFace. HuggingFace reported it to the FBI before OpenAI told it anything.

Europe's AI Act exempts pre-release testing. California said the hack "did not meet the threshold" for reporting. Congress won't vote on AI until next year.

Meanwhile, the EU revived warrantless scanning of private messages. ICE scans faces, and you can't decline. Police in 5,000 communities run Flock cameras, and a leaked AI tool finds your car by where it goes. No plate needed.

Governments can move fast. They move fast on you. Your messages, your face, your car, your liberty. 

My prediction: the labs keep their exemptions, everything becomes a "test" and the next surveillance laws get sold as AI safety.

How to launch a product in 2026:

1. Find a problem to solve
2. Work out the minimum viable solution
3. Get AI to make the solution
4. Get ready to launch
5. Think of extra feature to add
6. Get AI to add feature
7. Get ready to launch
8. Research competitors
9. Find 15 new features to add
10. Get AI to add features
11. Think of better way to do things
12. Get AI to remake things
13. Get ready to launch
14. Think of new problem to solve instead
15. Work out the minimum viable solution
16. Get AI to make the solution
17. Worry no one will buy
18. Worry no one even needs your product (even though you need it)
19. Think of new problem to solve instead

items.text:
AI decision making is getting cheaper.

but making those decisions trustworthy is a different problem.

I have been thinking about this after seeing a post from @kstellana about what TypeSafe is doing with Jev.

which is basically how you can break complex decisions into smaller ones, give the model relevant evidence, and get consistent results for almost nothing.

but it might come with a cost, that is the stakes changes.

For example :

Did an agent actually complete the task?

Should escrow release $20 or $20m?

did someone breach an agreement?

Yes when the cost of being wrong increases, cheap judgment alone isn't enough.

@GenLayer

Been looking at @BeldexCoin recent changes and they get more interesting the deeper you look past the headline.

The new V7.0.4 release touches several parts of the network: wallet and RPC work, validation, Proof-of-Stake, P2P communication, Flash Sync and the transaction pool.

There's also a new version of the Beldex explorer giving users a cleaner way to check the blockchain and look through network activity.

What stands out to me is how these updates are landing alongside the bigger conversation around AI agents, identity and privacy.

Beldex isn't just talking about where Web3 is going the team is building the infrastructure underneath it while the ecosystem keeps adding pieces around BDX.

I'll be watching closely how these technical improvements develop for the project.

𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗘𝗗 𝗕𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗪𝗜𝗗𝗧𝗛 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗢 𝗔 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗞𝗘𝗧

Most people think of BitTorrent as a way to share files.

The deeper idea is economic:

𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗜𝗙 𝗡𝗘𝗧𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗦 𝗖𝗢𝗨𝗟𝗗 𝗕𝗘 𝗣𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗘𝗗, 𝗦𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗘𝗗, 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗖𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗭𝗘𝗗?

BitTorrent's BTT design introduced an economic layer around bandwidth and storage resources, allowing service requesters and providers to transact using BTT.

𝗙𝗥𝗢𝗠 𝗣𝗘𝗘𝗥-𝗧𝗢-𝗣𝗘𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗢 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗖𝗘 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗞𝗘𝗧𝗦

BitTorrent Speed demonstrates the concept in practice.

When downloading, the client can automatically bid BTT to other users for faster speeds, while seeders can earn BTT for contributing bandwidth.

𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗥 → 𝗕𝗜𝗗 → 𝗕𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗪𝗜𝗗𝗧𝗛 → 𝗙𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗥 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The network turns an unused resource into something that can participate in an economic system.

𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗚𝗘 𝗙𝗜𝗧𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗔𝗠𝗘 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟

BTFS extends the resource-sharing concept toward decentralized storage.

Storage providers contribute capacity.

Users request storage and retrieval.

BTT provides an economic layer across supported services.

𝗖𝗔𝗣𝗔𝗖𝗜𝗧𝗬 → 𝗨𝗦𝗔𝗚𝗘 → 𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗜𝗖𝗘 → 𝗣𝗔𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧 → 𝗜𝗡𝗖𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗘

BTFS documentation and release notes also describe hosts setting storage prices and receiving BTT payments for providing storage.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚𝗚𝗘𝗥 𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗔

This is more than bandwidth pricing.

It is a model for turning distributed resources into economic infrastructure:

𝗕𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗪𝗜𝗗𝗧𝗛 → 𝗦𝗧𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗚𝗘 → 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗨𝗧𝗘 → 𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗜𝗖𝗘𝗦

The same philosophy can extend toward newer decentralized workloads, including distributed AI compute.

BTTInferGrid explores that direction by connecting distributed hardware with AI inference workloads.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗢𝗠𝗜𝗖 𝗟𝗢𝗢𝗣 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

Infrastructure needs providers.

Providers need demand.

Demand creates usage.

Usage can create economic activity.

Economic incentives can encourage continued participation.

𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗖𝗘 → 𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗜𝗖𝗘 → 𝗨𝗦𝗔𝗚𝗘 → 𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗨𝗘 → 𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗜𝗣𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

That is the bigger BitTorrent experiment.

Not simply distributing data.

𝗕𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗨𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗦 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗢 𝗨𝗦𝗘𝗙𝗨𝗟 𝗡𝗘𝗧𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞 𝗜𝗡𝗙𝗥𝗔𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗨𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘.
